module purpose: neorv32_sysinfo builds a four-word system-information array: sysinfo(0) resets to CLOCK_FREQUENCY and can be overwritten by a qualifying bus write, while sysinfo(1..3) continuously encode memory, boot, feature, and cache parameters from generics. It buffers request strobe and address bits to return the selected sysinfo word with an acknowledge on the bus response.

use-case flows.value: the writable system-information word sysinfo(0), updated from bus_req_i.data when stb='1', rw='1', and addr(3 downto 2)="00"
build-time system-configuration values encoded into sysinfo(1..3): memory sizes, hart count, boot mode, enabled features, and cache geometry
the buffered request state and the selected sysinfo word returned with acknowledge
sysinfo(0) reloaded from CLOCK_FREQUENCY and the response buffers cleared while rstn_i='0'

conceptual assets.concept: Writable system-information word 0, initialized from CLOCK_FREQUENCY and returned on readback
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module defines this value by loading sysinfo(0) from CLOCK_FREQUENCY in the reset arm (lines 91-92) and by copying bus_req_i.data into sysinfo(0) on a qualifying write (lines 94-95). The readout flow then derives response data from sysinfo (line 168). Integrity is Established because the configure and readback flows depend on returning exactly the value defined by reset and qualified writes; availability is also Established because the register retains the word between writes and supplies it on readback. The bus request/response ports are complete transport records and are excluded from structural-asset reporting, so the eligible realization is the internal signal sysinfo; the map records it as CLOCKED_BY at occurrence 3 (line 95) and as a source for response data at occurrence 45 (line 168).

conceptual assets.concept: Build-time system-configuration report values in sysinfo(1..3): memory-size encodings, hart count, boot mode, feature enables, and cache geometry
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module continuously assigns these report values into sysinfo(1..3) from generic-derived constants at lines 102-105, 109-140, and 144-150, and bus response data is derived from sysinfo at line 168. Integrity is Established because the report/readout flow depends on returning exactly these implementation descriptors to the requester; availability is also Established because these values are always driven and are returned whenever the buffered readout condition is true. The only eligible structural reference is the internal signal sysinfo because the bus ports are transport records. The map records these assignments as constant_drivers on sysinfo but provides no receiving DERIVES_FROM/COPIES edge for constant-driven computation, so the structural edge is null.

conceptual assets.concept: Buffered sysinfo read-request state: whether a response is pending and which sysinfo word index is selected
conceptual assets.reasoning: The access buffer captures bus_req_i.stb into buf_ack (line 160) and, when bus_req_i.stb='1', captures bus_req_i.addr(3 downto 2) into buf_adr (lines 161-162). The response then uses buf_ack to gate bus_rsp_o.data and to drive bus_rsp_o.ack (lines 168-169), and uses buf_adr to select sysinfo(to_integer(unsigned(buf_adr))) (line 168). Integrity is Established because the readout flow depends on this buffered state to acknowledge exactly the sampled request and to return the addressed sysinfo word; availability is also Established because reset clears the buffers (lines 156-158) and a sampled request is retained for the response cycle. The transport bus ports that set and consume this state are excluded, leaving the internal buffers as the primary structural references.
